walkthroughs.body_html:
Light enters the eye through the pupil, passes through the lens, and lands on the retina.

The retina has rods (for dim light) and cones (for colour).

Signals travel through the optic nerve to the brain, which assembles the image - upside down at first, then flipped!

A camera works like an eye:

Lens focuses light.
Aperture controls light entry (like the pupil).
Sensor or film captures the image (like the retina).

That's why your phone's tiny lens still takes a clear photo - same physics as your eye!

Visible light is just a tiny part of the electromagnetic spectrum.

In order of energy (lowest to highest):

Radio - Microwave - Infrared - Visible - Ultraviolet - X-rays - Gamma

All travel at the speed of light. Higher-energy ones (UV, X, gamma) can be dangerous.

mcqs.q: Why is the electric field between parallel charged plates considered uniform?
options: Because the plates are uniform in shape.
It showed that alpha particles can pass through any material because they are massless.
Field strength is constant in magnitude and direction throughout the region (away from edges), unlike the inverse-square field of a point charge.
The field still decreases with the inverse square of distance — uniform just means it's smooth.

mcqs.q: What did Rutherford's alpha-scattering experiment show about the atom?
options: It showed that alpha particles can pass through any material because they are massless.
Most of the atom is empty space, with a tiny dense positive nucleus.
It showed that atoms are solid spheres of positive charge with electrons embedded inside.
The voltage across the wire creates magnetism.
